The test image shows a soybean leaf with one prominent circular lesion: dark brown/black outer ring, light tan/cream center, and small scattered dark spots. This pattern with a distinct dark border and pale center strongly suggests Frogeye leaf spot.

Let me check reference images across 8 classes.
Good match — Frogeye shows circular spots with pale centers and dark borders. Let me check other candidates.
Cercospora here shows seed staining, not leaf lesions. Let me check Bacterial_Blight and Anthracnose.
Bacterial Blight shows angular lesions with yellow halos — different from the test image's circular, ringed lesion. Checking Anthracnose.
Anthracnose shows stem/pod damage here. Checking Phyllosticta leaf spot, which also causes circular lesions.
Phyllosticta shows irregular brown lesions, some circular but with brown centers. Let me check Frogeye more closely and Septoria.

This Frogeye reference strongly matches — circular lesions with pale centers and dark borders, some dropping out (shot-hole). Very similar to the test image lesion shape.

Let me check Septoria and one more class.
Septoria shows irregular brown spots on yellowing leaves — doesn't match. Checking Bacterial_Pustule.

All 8 views complete. 

**Summary of findings:**
- **Frogeye leaf spot** (refs 2 & 6): circular lesions with pale gray/cream centers and dark brown borders — matches the test image precisely, including the shot-hole tendency and scattered small spots
- **Bacterial Blight**: angular lesions with yellow halos — no match
- **Cercospora**: seed staining — no match  
- **Anthracnose**: stem/pod damage — no match
- **Phyllosticta**: irregular larger brown lesions — weaker match
- **Septoria**: irregular spots on yellowing leaves — no match
- **Bacterial Pustule**: mottled tissue close-up — no match

The test image lesion is a classic Frogeye leaf spot: circular, with a pale tan center and distinct dark brown ring border, on an otherwise green leaf with small scattered spots.
